taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and ITIS. Texas is part of the native range, but current review recovered only one exact project target-zone county.

evidence: Kew/POWO and ITIS accept Vitis palmata as native in Texas.
Travis County — Delta State University Herbarium documents a Vitis palmata specimen collected in Austin at the University of Texas.
Texas floristic records confirm the species elsewhere in eastern Texas, but those counties are outside the project's target-zone list.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Fewer than three exact target-zone counties are verified under the current taxon concept.
target_zone_range.guardrail: A single Travis specimen plus broad Texas nativity does not satisfy the three-target-county rule. Do not infer Hays/Williamson occurrence from proximity.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the stem before the fruit. Catbird grape has uniformly red, purplish-red or chestnut branchlets and usually deeply 3(–5)-lobed leaves with long-pointed lobes. The lower leaf surface is essentially glabrous, and it is a riverbank/slough/floodplain grape.
diagnostic_traits: branchlets uniformly red, purplish red or chestnut
branchlets glabrous or only very sparsely cobwebby
leaves usually deeply 3(–5)-lobed with long-acuminate tips
leaf undersides glabrous or nearly so
berries bluish black to black, 8–10 mm, slightly or not glaucous
associated with riverbanks, sloughs and alluvial floodplain woods

confusers.separator: V. berlandieri usually lacks uniformly red branchlets and has less deeply lobed leaves with some sparse lower-surface webbing plus more heavily glaucous fruit.
V. cinerea has hairy/cobwebby angled branchlets and hairier leaf undersides; V. palmata is much glabrier and red-stemmed.
Mustang grape has a dense white woolly leaf underside and generally broader, less consistently deeply lobed mature leaves.

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project-native taxon until three exact target-zone counties are verified under the current taxonomic concept.
